title: List-Coloring and Chromatic-Choosability -- A Dynamic Survey
summary: List-coloring, introduced independently by Vizing and by Erdős, Rubin, and Taylor in the 1970s, generalizes ordinary vertex coloring by assigning to each vertex its own set of admissible colors. A graph is chromatic-choosable if its list chromatic number equals its chromatic number. The previous survey on list-coloring by D R Woodall (2001), emphasized defective choosability, the list-coloring conjectures, and different methods used for list-coloring.
